## Open

### F-256 — The demo scenarios cannot authenticate, so the report stops at the login

> _2026-09-25 · demo/handler-test-poc · open_

`index.test.ts` plus tap plus scripts make the suite run (F-243), and the chain reaches the
handlers, but the first authenticated call returns 401 "missing authorization header". The login
step itself reports ok, because the codec.test helper (`testLoginTokenCreate`) resolves
`loginTokenCreate` inside the browser's own `testDispatch` rather than over the testClient backend —
no `/rpc/login/token/create` request appears in the log — so the MLE adapter never caches a token
and every later call sends no Authorization header. Calling `loginTokenCreate` directly from the
scenario, as `realm/blong-access` does, fails earlier and differently: "login > Error" from
`codec/adapter/jsonrpc/receive.ts`, because this suite's server loads no blong-server realm and
configures no `gateway.authorize`, while blong-access loads both (`srv` +
`access.authorization.list`). The 85-second hang that follows a failed step then trips tap's
timeout, so the three groups that would have passed never start.

Lesson: a scenario whose steps call handlers that live on the other platform is not "internal API
testing" — it needs the auth realm and an ordered login, or the handlers belong in the server test
layer. See the todo entry recorded beside this one.

### F-262 — A port 404 reads as a missing realm, but the route comes from blong-server

> _2026-09-25 · demo/handler-test-poc · open_

A realm-to-realm call that 404s reads as a missing realm, and in this suite it was not one. The
login mints a token by calling `access.credential.check`, and the run failed with `404 (Not Found)`
for `POST /rpc/ports/access/request` while the access mock was already loaded and its handlers were
registered.

The route is not the realm's to provide: `/rpc/ports/{namespace}/request` comes from the subject
dispatch that blong-server contributes, the way `orchestrator/subject/init.ts` only declares the
namespace. Adding `srv` to the suite is what turned the 404 into a working call.

The lesson: when a port 404s, check the platform for the dispatch before checking for the realm. The
suites that do this correctly (blong-marine, blong-access) load blong-server next to the realms they
call, which is easy to read as being about their own pages rather than about the ports.

Diagnosing this cost a detour through the login realm's internals, because the error names the
namespace the caller asked for and never distinguishes a missing realm from a missing route.

## Resolved

### F-243 — handler-test-poc has no test script, so blong-dev test crashes

> _2026-09-23 · demo/handler-test-poc · resolved_

The package has browser/server test handlers under `test/test/` and a `server.ts` that sets
`checkpointMode: 'test'`, but no `test` script and no `tap` dependency, so `blong-dev test` here
dies with `Cannot find package 'tap' imported from .../x` and then reports "tap produced no report
that could be parsed". Read as a failure, it is a trap: the handlers in this package are only
exercised through the suite that includes `demo/handler-test-poc` as a realm, not by running them
from the package.

Fixed: the package has index.test.ts, a test script, ci-test, tap and blong-gogo as dependencies,
and blong-dev test now boots both platforms, discovers the five groups and runs them. What they do
not do yet is finish, which is a different defect: the login token never reaches the MLE adapter,
recorded as a friction and a todo in the same package.

### F-258 — Option 1 for the demo scenarios does not fix the login

> _2026-09-25 · demo/handler-test-poc · resolved_

Option 1 of T-149 (order the login) was implemented and it does not fix the run. Three findings,
each reproduced against the demo package.

There is no race to fix. `TestExecutor._executeSteps` awaits a nested array inline ("Nested step
group — wait for current batch first"), and the login helper returns exactly such an array, so the
login step completes before the following step is even enqueued. The 401 was never the first call
overtaking the login.

The helper's login produces no token. A probe step reading it resolves in about 4 ms to nothing, so
`testLoginTokenCreate`'s inner step returns null/undefined: the login call it makes yields nothing
rather than a token.

The direct route is not callable from the demo. Replacing the helper with the scenario's own
`loginTokenCreate({username: 'test', password: 'test'}, $meta)` step — the pattern
`realm/blong-access` uses — throws `remote.noMeta: $meta not passed to method: login.token.create`:
the call reaches the remote dispatch with a single argument, so the trailing `$meta` is dropped
somewhere between the scenario's handler proxy and the port. Adding `login` to
`order.testDispatch`'s `imports` changes neither symptom.

Declaring the dependency (the actual option 1 edit: `await login` as the first statement of the
first authenticated step) makes things worse: a 30 ms 401 becomes a 26 s timeout, so awaiting that
step's promise never settles. An isolated probe in `core/blong-chain` proves the executor is not at
fault — a step inside a nested group is awaitable by a later step, in 2.4 ms — so the hang belongs
to the demo's setup, most likely because the step the helper registers is not the step name the
scenario resolves.

Lesson: the blocker is the login binding through the demo's realm-level `order.testDispatch`. A
scenario step cannot call `login.token.create` the way blong-access's steps can, and that is why the
token never reaches the MLE backend adapter. Option 2 (load the blong-server realm and
`gateway.authorize` the way blong-access does, plus the dependency) or option 3 (move the scenario
handlers so the run is in-process) are the routes that address the cause; option 1 alone cannot.

Resolved, and the entry's own caution held: with the access mock and srv loaded the awaited login is
what makes the scenarios pass, and the hang it warned about (F-260) was real while the login could
not succeed.
